note: The validation artifacts this repository measures its conformance against. Every
reference here is immutable and every fetch is checked against the digest beside it
before a single validation result is produced. A branch name is not a pin: each entry
names a git commit SHA, which is content-addressed over the whole tree at that commit,
so the same URL can never serve different bytes. Nothing in this list is committed to
this repository; the harness fetches it into a gitignored working directory at run time.
Each sha256 was computed from the bytes of the first fetch, recorded here, and is
re-verified on every run. To move a pin: change the commit, run pnpm conformance, and
take the digest it refuses with, having first read the diff between the two commits.

corpus.title: HL7 C-CDA-Examples, the public R2.1 sample set
integrityNote: The digest below is over the archive's CONTENT, not over its gzip bytes: the sorted
list of one 'sha256  relative/path' line per .xml entry, newline-joined and newline-
terminated. GitHub generates the tarball on demand and has changed its compression
settings before, so the packaging bytes are not a sound pin while the content at a
commit SHA is fixed forever. A single changed byte in a single sample moves this
digest, which is the property AC-7 needs.

cdaSchema.title: CDA R2 XML schema, the SDTC-extended tree
schemaNote: The SDTC tree rather than schema/normative, and the difference is the whole reason the
pin names it. buildCcda emits {urn:hl7-org:sdtc}deceasedInd on a family history relative,
an HL7-approved SDO extension the parser reads back; the normative schema declares no
extension elements at all, so it rejects that document as structurally invalid while the
Schematron, which is written against C-CDA R2.1, says nothing about it. The repository's
own README states that 'the schema/extensions folder contains an SDTC folder which has the
updated CDA schema with all SDTC extensions that are approved by HL7'. Measuring against
the normative tree would have meant either publishing a schema failure for a conformant
document or dropping an extension a consumer relies on. The file list below is the
transitive closure of the entry point's own includes and imports, nothing more.
